b2-41.title: Dress and Manners Abroad
b2-41.story: Anna's university held an international evening, and Lisa insisted they should learn the right [[etiquette]] first. A classmate from India arrived in a bright green [[sari]] and showed them how the long fabric is wrapped. Ira had borrowed a silk [[kimono]] from her aunt, although she kept stepping on its hem. A visiting professor wore a neat blue [[turban]] and patiently answered everyone's questions about it. At the Japanese stand, a short film explained that a [[geisha]] trains for years in music, dance and conversation. Later, at the French café corner, a student dressed as a waiter bowed and said, "[[Madame|madame]], your pancakes are ready." Anna was so surprised that she bowed back, and the whole table laughed. By the end of the night, she decided that good manners mostly mean being curious and kind.

b2-42.title: A City Break in Prague
b2-42.story: Anna and Max finally booked a [[city break]] in Prague for the long weekend. Their [[tour agent]] found a cheap hotel and sent them a list of every [[must-see]] in the old town. On the first morning, they picked up free maps at the [[info center]] near the main square. Then they jumped on a [[hop-on hop-off]] bus so they could see the whole city before lunch. In the castle museum, Max rented an [[audio guide]] but kept pausing it to take photos. Later they rode the old [[funicular]] up the hill and watched the sunset over the red roofs. Their last evening was a [[food tour]], which turned out to be the best part of the trip. On the train home, Max admitted that he had tried four kinds of dumplings in one night.

b2-43.title: The Night Before the Flight
b2-43.story: The night before her flight to Lisbon, Anna was packing while she chatted with Max on video. She had already installed an [[eSIM]], so she wouldn't need to buy a local card. Max sent her a [[life hack]]: roll your clothes instead of folding them to save space. Anna packed her new [[action camera]] for the surfing lesson she had booked. She also squeezed in a [[selfie stick]], even though Max teased her about it. "Your phone already has a fifty [[megapixel]] camera," he said. "Just make sure the [[autofocus]] is on this time, unlike last summer." At the airport, the flight was delayed, and Dad used his travel card to get them into the [[business lounge]]. The Wi-Fi there was terrible, so Anna used her phone as a [[hotspot]] to message Max. She sent him a blurry selfie anyway, just to annoy him.

b2-44.title: A Week by the Sea
b2-44.story: Lisa's family invited Anna to spend a week by the sea in Greece. They stayed at a small family [[guesthouse]] with a view of the harbor. Next door was an expensive [[eco hotel]] with solar panels and a garden on the roof. During the day, the girls lay on sunbeds at the [[beach club]] and bought cold lemonade at the [[beach bar]]. One afternoon they walked too far along the coast and saw a sign for a [[nudist]] beach, so they quickly turned around, giggling. Lisa's uncle was a member of the local [[yacht club]] and took them sailing on Thursday. That evening, the hotel next door held a [[pool party]], and the music was so loud they could hear it from their room. On their last night, they went to a [[beach party]] with a bonfire and danced until midnight. Anna promised herself she would come back next summer.

b2-45.title: Shopping for a New Car
b2-45.story: Anna's dad had been driving the same old [[hatchback]] for twelve years, and it was finally time for a new car. On Saturday, the whole family went to the [[auto show]] at the expo center to look at electric models. Dad read every [[crash test]] result before he would even sit in a car. Taras ignored the family cars and ran straight to the giant [[monster truck]] on display. Near the exit, members of a [[biker club]] in leather jackets were showing off their shiny old motorcycles. On the way home, a warning light came on, and the [[speedometer]] suddenly stopped working. Dad drove slowly to the nearest [[auto center]], where a mechanic fixed a loose wire in twenty minutes. While they waited, Taras watched an [[excavator]] digging across the road and said it was better than the whole show.

b2-46.title: Mama's New Home Office
b2-46.story: When Anna's mama started working remotely, she turned the spare bedroom into a [[home office]]. Her old [[laptop]] was too slow for video calls, so she bought a used [[desktop]] with a big screen. Taras helped her connect every [[cable]], although he mixed up two of them at first. She also ordered a small [[microphone]] because her colleagues said she sounded like she was underwater. The webcam had a digital [[zoom]], which Mama accidentally used in her first meeting, filling the screen with her nose. The internet kept dropping, so Dad called their [[provider]], who told him to move the [[router]] closer to her room. By Friday, the whole [[setup]] was working perfectly. Then the power went out, and Mama spent the afternoon working [[offline]] on documents she had saved earlier.

b2-47.title: A Bad Day for Max's Laptop
b2-47.story: On Monday morning, Max's [[task manager]] app reminded him that his essay was due at noon. Ten minutes later, his laptop froze in the middle of the last paragraph. It turned out to be a [[glitch]] caused by last night's [[update]] to his writing app. A [[reset]] of the app didn't help, but luckily he had made a [[backup]] on Sunday. Sofia, who studies IT, said the real problem was his old [[hardware]] and that he needed a memory [[upgrade]]. She also showed him a keyboard [[shortcut]] that saves the file whenever he presses it. Then the printer announced that it needed a new ink [[cartridge]]. So Max ran to the library and used the [[scanner]] to send his handwritten notes to the teacher. He handed in the essay five minutes before the deadline.

b2-48.title: Grandpa Goes Online
b2-48.story: Anna's grandpa wanted to find a recipe online, so she sat down to help him. He wasn't sure what a [[web browser]] was, so she explained that it is the program you use to open websites. When she opened her favorite [[browser]], a [[pop-up]] about cookies appeared, and Grandpa nearly closed the whole window. Next they checked his email, which was full of [[spam]] promising free money. Anna deleted it all and showed him how to type a web address, with a [[slash]] before the page name. They found a cooking [[wiki]] where thousands of people share family recipes. To save his favorite ones, Grandpa had to become a registered [[user]] and fill in his [[profile]]. He proudly chose a photo of his garden instead of his face. Then Anna used a [[template]] to make a neat recipe card for Grandma's birthday. She added a [[QR code]] to the back, and Grandma laughed when it opened Grandpa's new page.
